title: Mom’s French Toast with Maple-Butter Syrup
description: Paula Deen’s baked French toast casserole: thick slices of French bread soaked overnight in custard, baked under a buttery pecan praline topping, and served with warm maple syrup with butter melted in.
author: Mom
time: 20 minutes, plus overnight soaking and 45 minutes baking
story: Mom makes Paula Deen’s French toast casserole. The oval slices of French bread keep their crunchy crust edges, and she makes sure it always has its nut topping, pecans or walnuts. We pour maple syrup with butter melted in over the top.
imageAlt: Golden French toast slices with maple-butter syrup and toasted walnuts on a floral plate.

steps.title: Slice the bread
steps.text: Cut the French bread into 20 slices about 1 inch thick. Save any extra for garlic toast or breadcrumbs.
steps.why: Thick slices of a long loaf come out oval, and each keeps a ring of crust that turns crunchy in the oven.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Lay the slices in the dish in 2 rows, overlapping them.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, half-and-half, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until blended but not frothy. Pour it over the bread, making sure every slice is covered, and spoon some between the slices.
steps.why: Whisking until frothy traps air that bakes into a spongy layer. Custard spooned between the slices soaks the middle of the dish, not only the top.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Cover the dish with foil and refrigerate it overnight.
steps.why: French bread is dense. A night in the fridge lets the custard soak all the way through, so the middle bakes up like bread pudding.

steps.title: Make the praline topping
steps.text: The next morning, heat the oven to 350°F. Stir together the softened butter, brown sugar, pecans or walnuts, corn syrup, cinnamon, and nutmeg, and spread it evenly over the bread.
steps.why: Use the full 2 sticks of butter. With less, the topping won’t melt together into a crisp praline crust.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for about 45 minutes, until puffed and lightly golden.

steps.title: Warm the syrup
steps.text: While it bakes, warm the maple syrup and butter in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter melts. Stir and keep it warm.
steps.why: Warm syrup holds the melted butter in, and it soaks into the French toast instead of sitting on top.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm, with the maple-butter syrup poured over the top.

notes.Paula Deen’s syrup: Paula Deen serves hers with a warm raspberry syrup: 1 cup raspberry preserves, 3 tablespoons water, and 2 tablespoons raspberry liqueur, heated until thinned. We use maple syrup with butter melted in.
notes.Make ahead: Assemble it the night before, then add the topping and bake in the morning.

source.name: Paula Deen’s Baked French Toast Casserole with Praline Topping
